Typically sulfonyl chloride is R-SO2-Cl, then amine attaches. Here we have R1 = fused aromatic system, R2 = 4-fluorophenyl. So we need sulfonyl chloride with both aryl groups attached: i.e., 4-fluorophenyl-(fused aromatic)-sulfonyl chloride. That's not typical; usually sulfonyl chloride has one R group. So we can think of sulfonyl chloride derived from fluorophenyl sulfonyl chloride (4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Then react with an aniline (the fused aromatic amine). So disconnection: break S-N bond, giving 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride and the aniline (aryl amine). That seems plausible.

So we can further disconnect the piperazine carbamate via carbamate formation (tert-butyl chloroformate) with piperazine amine.
